stem.text: A particle moves in the xy-plane so that its position at time t is \( \left(x(t), y(t)\right) = \left( \frac{t^{2}}{2} - \sin{\left(t \right)} + 6,\ - \frac{t^{3}}{3} + 3 t \right) \) for \( 0 \le t \le 2 \). Using a calculator where needed, find all times t in the open interval \( 0 < t < 2 \) at which the particle is moving toward the y-axis. Give a reason for your answer, and give any decimal endpoint correct to three decimal places.

answer_key.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 0.739 \), because \( x(t) \) and \( x'(t) \) have opposite signs there.

worked_solution.text: Since \( \sin t \le 1 \), \( x(t) \ge 5 \) for every t, so \( x(t) \) is positive and the particle stays on one side of the y-axis.

The particle moves toward the y-axis when \( x(t) \) and \( x'(t) \) have opposite signs, that is, when \( x'(t) = t - \cos{\left(t \right)} < 0 \). A calculator gives \( x'(t) = 0 \) at \( t \approx 0.739 \), with \( x'(t) \) negative before that time and the opposite sign after it.
So the particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 0.739 \), because there \( x(t) > 0 \) and \( x'(t) < 0 \), so its distance from the y-axis, \( |x(t)| \), is decreasing.
worked_solution.rule_named: sign analysis of the velocity component

options.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for \( 0 < t < 0.739 \), because \( x(t) \) is positive there.
options.derivation: the right times given but justified by the sign of x(t) instead of the sign of its rate

options.label: The particle moves toward the y-axis for no t with \( 0 < t < 2 \), because \( x(t) \) is positive there.
options.derivation: the sign of the coordinate read as the direction of motion, so a positive x(t) taken to mean the particle never approaches
